From: Fenech, Anthony 
Sent: Saturday, August 24, 2019 11:51 AM
To: Thomas, Christopher <cdthomas@freepress.com>
Subject: Tweet section
I think I went from three grafs (Tweet) to five with further background.
In a tweet Thursday, Verlander said Fenech showed “unethical” past behavior.
The claims stem from a pair of tweets Fenech posted on Aug. 22, 2017, shortly after joining a conversation between Verlander and Al Kaline in the Tigers’ clubhouse at Comerica Park.

After talking off-the-record with Verlander at his locker about an unrelated topic, Fenech walked up to the pair and engaged in a conversation about Verlander watching the solar eclipse, asking him questions about the experience.

That night, Fenech was informed by a Tigers media relations official that Verlander was unhappy with the tweets. The next day, Verlander expressed those thoughts in a profanity-laced tirade inside the Tigers dugout in front of multiple players and coaches.

The next time they spoke, in a postgame media scrum on Aug. 25 in Chicago, Verlander told Fenech, “You should stop,” in response to a question about what was said during a mid-game altercation with Victor Martinez the previous day, before walking out of the scrum.
In his final start as a Tiger, on Aug. 30 in Denver, Verlander did not answer two game-related questions from Fenech in a postgame media scrum.

Though the pair spoke on two occasions with no issues over the next year – at the 2017 World Series and in Houston prior to Verlander’s first start against the Tigers on July 14, 2018 – the breaking point appears to be a Sept. 12, 2018 interview that went on and off the record and ended with a disagreement about the context surrounding the exchange of a phone number.

Fenech had been assigned to ask Verlander about a Bleacher Report story published Aug. 9, 2018, in which Verlander said the Tigers “misdiagnosed” an injury in 2015. The Free Press was the first Detroit media outlet to ask Verlander about the comments.
